newsitem.title: USA: USDA adjusts quality factor in world rice price.
newsitem.headline: USDA adjusts quality factor in world rice price.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said its latest world rice prices reflected an adjustment to the quality difference factor.

This factor in the world price calculation adjusts foreign prices to a standardized U.S. grade and quality basis. USDA uses a number of grades of rice from a number of countries to set the world price.
The department said in the future, adjustments to this factor, if required, will be made the first Tuesday of each quarter.

The department previously has not announced adjustments to the quality difference factor. It said it would now do so to help producers predict the timing of world price adjustments based on the quality difference and other technical factors.
USDA earlier reported the prevailing world market prices of milled rice, loan rate basis, effective from today as follows:
-- Long grain whole kernels, 13.28 cts per lb, versus
-- Medium grain whole kernels, 11.41 cts, versus 11.43.
-- Short grain whole kernels, 11.39 cts, versus 11.41.
